chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Khadir ibn Amr al-Nakha'i, who said:

One of the two Imams (peace be upon them) said regarding a man who has a debt due from another man who denies it: If he (the creditor) asks him to swear an oath, it is not for him to take anything from him after the swearing; and if he leaves it and does not ask him to swear, then he (the creditor) is upon his right.

key_terms.اسْتَحْلَفَهُ: he asked him to swear an oath

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a debtor denies a debt and swears an oath?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the mechanism of *istihlaf* (administering an oath) as a legal proof in Shia jurisprudence for settling debt disputes. It highlights the creditor's strategic choice: demanding an oath transfers the burden of proof to the debtor, and a successful oath discharges the debt, whereas withholding the oath preserves the creditor's original claim. This principle underscores the Shia emphasis on procedural justice and the evidentiary weight of oaths in civil transactions.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Hazar Bin Amro and Al Nakhaie who said,

‘One of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) said regarding the man who happens to have some wealth for him, so he takes it: ‘If he (the debtor) swears, so it is not for him (the creditor) that he takes from him after the swearing of the oath; and if he neglects it and does not swear, so he (the creditor) is upon his right’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid from Khidr ibn ‘Amr al-Nakha’iy who has said the following: “

About the case of a man to whom another person owes a certain amount of assets but denies such liability one of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘If he (creditor) makes him (the debtor) to take an oath, thereafter he (the creditor) is not entitled to take anything from him (the debtor), but if he does not make him to take an oath his right remains enforced upon the debtor.’”
